thread:
tayla (sec): Quick alert: we received a vulnerability report for our internal tokenbroker service (TBKR). Issue: improper validation of refresh token nonce could allow replay of a revoked refresh token for ~30s after revocation.

omar (infra): Confirmed on staging. Affects tokenbroker versions <= 1.8.2 when using clustered cache.

jade (sdk): What should SDKs do? Any client changes?

tayla (sec): Immediate mitigations: 1) hotpatch tokenbroker to 1.8.3 (fixes nonce check) within 4 hours for hosted and dedicated control planes; 2) enable strict revocation mode by setting TBKR_STRICT_REVOKE=true (may add small latency); 3) rotate any refresh tokens used in automation.

ops-bot: Deployment: tokenbroker-canary -> v1.8.3 by omar at 2026-04-12T14:12:09Z. Status: success.

omar (infra): Commands: `redwood-admin tokenbroker status --cluster <name>` and `redwood-admin tokenbroker upgrade --to 1.8.3 --cluster <name>`.

jade (sdk): We'll push SDK patch to gracefully handle 401-with-retry and short-circuit reauth. SDK release planned in 1 hour.

tayla (sec): Please scan repos and CI for long-lived refresh tokens used in automation: `grep -R "refresh_token" --exclude-dir=.git || true`. Rotate any found.

omar (infra): Note: Dedicated customers will get a notice and a recommended upgrade package. Private customers: contact sec-team for guidance and backports.

tayla (sec): Post-action: we will require all teams to submit a short confirmation in this thread when their tokenbroker instances are patched and any automation tokens rotated. We'll compile a report for leadership.

ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: patch-confirmation due by 2026-04-12T18:00:00Z. Use `/security patch report --service tokenbroker --cluster <name>` to submit.
